content: The American College of Physicians (ACP) is a national organization composed of internists, who are physicians specializing in the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of illnesses affecting adults. With over 119,000 members, ACP is the largest medical-specialty organization and the second-largest physician group in the United States. The organization provides resources and advocacy for its members practicing internal medicine and related subspecialties. Members are also engaged in medical education, research, and administrative roles. Membership includes medical students, residents, and fellows. The mission of the ACP is to improve the quality and effectiveness of healthcare by promoting excellence and professionalism in the practice of medicine. Founded in 1915, the ACP was established to advance the science and practice of medicine. In 1998, it merged with the American Society of Internal Medicine (ASIM), which was founded in 1956 to address the economic aspects of medicine. From 1998 to 2003, the organization was known as ACP-ASIM before reverting to its original name, the American College of Physicians. The ACP is governed by a Board of Regents, elected by its members. This board is supported by a network of committees and the ACP Board of Governors, which consists of 79 elected Governors representing chapters and regions in the United States, Canada, Central and South America, and Japan. The ACP also sponsors the Council of Subspecialty Societies, which represents 25 subspecialty societies and internal medicine organizations. Additionally, the ACP is represented in various national organizations, including the American Medical Association and the Council of Medical Specialty Societies. Membership in the ACP is categorized into several levels: Medical Student, Associate, Member, Fellow (FACP), Honorary Fellow, and Master (MACP). Fellowship and Mastership are distinctions awarded to members who demonstrate outstanding achievements in internal medicine. Fellows are nominated by their peers, endorsed by local chapter leadership, and reviewed by a national credentials subcommittee. Masters are selected annually from among the Fellows for this highly selective honor. Affiliate membership is available to physician assistants who are Fellows of the American Academy of Physician Assistants. Membership is otherwise restricted to physicians and medical students with an interest in internal medicine. While board certification in internal medicine is not required, potential members must be board eligible. Internists complete a three-year internal medicine training program after medical school, focusing on the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases primarily affecting adults. Subspecialty internists undergo an additional one to three years of training in fields such as cardiology, endocrinology, geriatrics, nephrology, gastroenterology, and infectious diseases. The ACP publishes the Annals of Internal Medicine, a bi-monthly journal that is one of the most-cited medical journals globally. The ACP Journal Club summarizes key clinical articles for internists from over 100 medical journals. The ACP Observer is a monthly news magazine for internists, and ACP Medicine is a continually updated, evidence-based reference for internal medicine. The ACP also publishes various books on healthcare and medical practice. Its public policy office monitors and responds to issues affecting public health and medical practice, developing policy statements and engaging with legislative and administrative sectors of government. The ACP Center for Ethics and Professionalism promotes understanding of ethical and professionalism issues in medicine to enhance patient care by upholding the highest ethical standards. The ACP Foundation supports the organization's mission and public health through programs in education, research, service, and professionalism. The ACP offers extensive educational and informational resources. Its continuing medical education programs include the Annual Session, a national scientific meeting with over 260 presentations; the Medical Knowledge Self-Assessment Program (MKSAP), now in its 13th edition; postgraduate board review courses; recertification courses; and chapter/regional meetings. For future internists, the ACP provides education and career information, produces MKSAP for Students, and administers an In-Training Examination for residents. Electronic resources include PIER (Physicians’ Information and Education Resource), a web-based decision-support tool offering evidence-based guidance in over 400 clinical areas, as well as MKSAP 13 and its updates. The ACP also provides a PDA portal on its website and Clinical Skills Teaching Modules to bring proven teaching techniques to classrooms. The ACP Practice Management Center offers members practical guides, management tools, and personalized advice to navigate the modern healthcare environment. The Medical Laboratory Evaluation Program (MLE) provides proficiency testing for laboratories in the U.S. and abroad. The ACP also publishes the Doctors for Adults® patient education website and offers free patient education brochures and videos/DVDs for physicians to raise awareness and educate their patients and communities. The website is reviewed by ACP physicians and contains no commercial endorsements. In 2007, the ACP launched its Diabetes Portal, an interactive resource for patients and clinicians.
